concept: SMAppService login items and privileged helpers for Mac App Store versus Developer ID
summary: Source-anchored research for SMAppService login items and privileged helpers for Mac App Store versus Developer ID. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: SMAppService requires that when a sandboxed app registers a daemon, that daemon is itself sandboxed. Apple DTS called this a deliberate change, enforced in macOS 14.4 and not listed in the release notes. An earlier restriction appeared in macOS 14.2. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2024-03-01)

A Mac App Store app cannot bundle an unsandboxed privileged helper: Apple DTS states all code shipped via the MAS must be sandboxed, and SMJobBless was never usable from a sandboxed app. DTS advises shipping the privileged daemon as a separate product (installer package or separate app that uses SMAppService), downloaded outside the MAS. (high confidence)
SMAppService.agent installs a per-user LaunchAgent only (current user, ~/Library/LaunchAgents); the API cannot install an agent for all users (Apple DTS). (medium confidence)

A helper-app login item (SMAppService.loginItem(identifier:)) must be bundled at MyApp.app/Contents/Library/LoginItems/Helper.app. The older SMLoginItemSetEnabled is deprecated from macOS 13. Status 78 (EX_CONFIG) means launchd rejected the job plist; a stale Launch Services database from many dev builds is a common cause. (medium confidence)

SMAppService.Status has four values: notRegistered, enabled, requiresApproval, notFound. A user can disable the item in System Settings > Login Items, which leaves it disallowed in the background-task database. The app should read status and prompt rather than assume success. (medium confidence)

Under the same restriction, sandboxed daemons on macOS 14.4 may not set StandardInputPath, StandardOutputPath or StandardErrorPath in their launchd plist; registration fails if they do. (low confidence) (verified as of 2024-03-01)

App Review Guideline 2.4.5 forbids MAS apps from requesting escalation to root or using setuid (v), from auto-launching or running code at startup or login without consent (iii), and from downloading or installing additional code or standalone apps (iv). Login items need an explicit user opt-in; root helpers are rejected. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-02)

SMAppService daemons and agents live inside the app bundle: the daemon plist at Contents/Library/LaunchDaemons/<id>.plist, with the executable referenced by a bundle-relative path. Registering a daemon requires user approval in System Settings, then admin authentication. After approval, re-registering needs no further authentication. (medium confidence)

SMAppService.mainApp (macOS 13+) registers the app itself as a login item with no helper bundle. Secondary sources describe it as sandbox and App Store compatible. Not checked against Apple's reference page. (low confidence)

Developer ID twin build: a non-sandboxed build can bundle a privileged daemon, register it with SMAppService.daemon (macOS 13+), and run it as root after user approval. The MAS build should omit this and use only mainApp or loginItem. The two builds need separate entitlements and targets. (medium confidence)
